title: Dinner at a restaurant
goal: Navigate the multi-course Italian menu, order each course, and ask for the bill without any confusion about tipping.
bekal: read a menu and understand the order of courses
ask for the bill and understand what *coperto* is

dialogs.title: Dialogo — Una cena in trattoria
dialogs.intro: A trattoria is a family restaurant, simpler and cheaper than a *ristorante*. Budi and Giulia are having dinner.

lines.speaker: Cameriere:
lines.id: Good evening. Do you have a reservation?

lines.speaker: Giulia:
lines.text: Sì, un tavolo per due a nome Rossi.
lines.id: Yes, a table for two under Rossi.
lines.literal: yes, a table for two at name Rossi.

lines.speaker: Cameriere:
lines.id: Please, have a seat. Here's the menu.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: Thank you. What do you recommend?

lines.speaker: Cameriere:
lines.text: Stasera i tortellini sono ottimi. Fatti in casa.
lines.id: Tonight the tortellini are excellent. Homemade.
lines.literal: tonight the tortellini are excellent. made in house.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Allora per me i tortellini. E come secondo?
lines.id: Then the tortellini for me. And for the main course?
lines.literal: then for me the tortellini. and as second?

lines.speaker: Cameriere:
lines.text: Il pesce del giorno è branzino al forno.
lines.id: The fish of the day is baked sea bass.
lines.literal: the fish of-the day is sea-bass at-the oven.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Perfetto, prendo quello. Con un contorno di verdure.
lines.id: Perfect, I'll have that. With a side of vegetables.
lines.literal: perfect, I-take that. with a side of vegetables.

lines.speaker: Giulia:
lines.text: Per me solo un primo: risotto ai funghi. Non ho molta fame.
lines.id: Just a first course for me: mushroom risotto. I'm not very hungry.
lines.literal: for me only a first: risotto at-the mushrooms. not I-have much hunger.

lines.speaker: Giulia:
lines.text: Una bottiglia d'acqua naturale e mezzo litro di vino rosso della casa.
lines.id: A bottle of still water and half a liter of the house red.
lines.literal: a bottle of-water natural and half liter of wine red of-the house.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: E dopo, il conto per favore. Insieme, non separato.
lines.id: And afterward, the bill please. Together, not separate.
lines.literal: and after, the bill for favor. together, not separate.

notes: **The Italian menu comes in courses, and nobody has to order them all.** *Antipasto* (starter), *primo* (pasta, risotto, soup), *secondo* (meat or fish), *contorno* (side vegetables), *dolce* (dessert). Ordering just a *primo* like Giulia is perfectly normal.
**The contorno is ordered separately.** The main course arrives alone on the plate — vegetables or potatoes don't come with it automatically. This surprises many newcomers.
**Per me** is the shortest way to order: *per me i tortellini* = "the tortellini for me". No verb needed at all. Italian waiters hear this more often than full sentences.
**Cosa mi consiglia?** = "What do you recommend?" At a family restaurant this always gets an honest answer, and often the best dish of the evening.

**Coperto is a cover charge, not a tip.** One to three euros per person, listed on the menu, for bread and the table setting. It's mandatory and official. Extra tipping isn't expected in Italy; rounding up is more than enough.
**Vino della casa** is the house wine — poured from the barrel, sold by the quarter, half, or full liter. Much cheaper than a bottle and usually quite good.
**Il conto, per favore.** In Italy the bill never comes on its own; waiting silently can last until closing time. Asking for it isn't rude — it's the only way.
**Avete prenotato** and *fatti in casa* use a past form you'll learn in unit 19. For now, just recognize them as whole phrases.

grammars.title: Ordering — patterns that will last you a lifetime
body: Four patterns, from shortest to fullest. All of them are polite.
after: *Mi porta* literally means "you bring me", said as a question. The tone of voice makes it polite, not any extra word.

grammars.title: Bere — the verb "to drink"
body: Irregular and very common. Notice that the stem changes from *be-* to *bev-*.
after: *Da bere* means "to drink" — the waiter's standard question. Its partner is *da mangiare* (to eat): *Qualcosa da mangiare?*

What's usually in it
rows: prosciutto e melone, bruschetta, affettati misti
insalata mista, patate al forno, verdure grigliate, spinaci

blocks.title: Phrases that will save your dinner
items: *Non mangio carne di maiale.* — I don't eat pork.
*C'è del maiale in questo piatto?* — Is there pork in this dish?
*Sono allergico ai frutti di mare.* — I'm allergic to seafood.
*Senza formaggio, per favore.* — No cheese, please.
*Il conto, per favore.* — The bill, please.
*Posso pagare con la carta?* — Can I pay by card?

blocks.text: If you don't eat pork, learn the two middle phrases by heart: pork sneaks into many Italian dishes through the back door — *prosciutto*, *pancetta*, *guanciale*, *salame*, *speck*, *lardo*, *salsiccia*, *mortadella* are all pork, even though none of them says *maiale*.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the correct form of bere.
Match each dish to its menu section. Write: antipasto, primo, secondo, contorno, or dolce.
Put the words in the right order.

answers: Un tavolo per due, per favore. — Che cosa mi consiglia? — Per me risotto ai funghi. — Una bottiglia d'acqua naturale. — Non mangio carne di maiale. — Il conto, per favore.
